name: Copilot Money
tagline: Personal finance app for spending, budgets, investments, and net worth

pricing.notes: Apple App Store pricing checked 2026-07-30; monthly subscription listed at $13 and yearly at $95.

tiers.name: Copilot Money
tiers.limits: All product features; 1 household subscription; no feature-based paid tiers

pricing.freeTierCaps: no free tier; interactive test drive before signup, then 7-day free trial

verdictSummary: A beautiful spending dashboard can be vibecoded, but Copilot's bank/investment sync, categorization, native Apple apps, and data-security posture are the product.
coreLoopDIY: Import bank/CSV data, categorize transactions with rules/LLM, show budgets, investments, and net-worth charts.
whyPeopleStillPay: They pay because the app feels native and current financial data appears automatically.

priorArt.name: Actual Budget
priorArt.desc: Open-source budgeting app; good starting point for a DIY personal finance workflow.

alternatives.name: Wealthfolio
alternatives.desc: Portfolio, net worth, spending and budgets on your own device; automatic broker sync is the paid convenience.

facts.install: Native desktop or iOS app, or the official Docker image/Compose deployment for web mode
facts.dataFormat: Desktop and self-hosted modes use a local SQLite database (the web server exposes a configurable app.db path); optional Wealthfolio Connect and encrypted device sync send selected holdings/account data through the vendor service.
facts.gapVsPaid: Wealthfolio cannot match Copilot's turnkey US account and card aggregation, automatic categorization, transaction cleanup, and consistently polished mobile-first daily-money workflow without paid sync.

alternatives.name: Money Manager Ex
alternatives.desc: A local ledger with budgets, reports and investments; the interface has no subscription budget.

facts.install: Native or portable desktop package for Windows, macOS, or Linux; mobile builds are also published
facts.dataFormat: Accounts and transactions live in a user-chosen local SQLite .mmb database, with optional database encryption; CSV, QIF, and other interchange formats are available.
facts.gapVsPaid: Money Manager Ex is a manual desktop ledger with a dated interface, not Copilot's automatically synced, mobile-first view of spending, investments, subscriptions, and net worth.

alternatives.name: GnuCash
alternatives.desc: Spending, budgets and investments in a serious double-entry desktop; simplicity did not make the balance sheet.

facts.install: Native desktop installer or operating-system package
facts.dataFormat: The default book is a local compressed XML .gnucash file; SQLite, MySQL, and PostgreSQL backends are optional, but the documentation warns that database storage does not make GnuCash a true multi-user application.
facts.gapVsPaid: GnuCash demands double-entry bookkeeping and manual imports, giving up Copilot's automatic account aggregation, approachable categorization, mobile polish, and unified investment dashboard.

alternatives.name: KMyMoney
alternatives.desc: Budgets, investments and cash-flow forecasts on the desktop; delight was not in the KDE requirements.

facts.install: Install a distribution package, Flatpak/AppImage, or the published Windows/macOS desktop build
facts.dataFormat: The normal .kmy file is compressed XML on the user's disk and can be GPG-encrypted; KMyMoney also supports SQL storage and imports such as QIF, OFX, and GnuCash XML.
facts.gapVsPaid: KMyMoney's desktop workflow and uneven bank connectivity are much less automatic and polished than Copilot's account aggregation, categorization, subscription detection, and mobile net-worth view.

notes: Good Apple-native example; core is easy, polish/data sync is sticky.
prompt:
Build me a personal finance dashboard to replace Copilot Money. Requirements:

- Local web app: Node + Express + better-sqlite3, charts with Chart.js, no
  build step.
- No bank APIs: I drop CSV exports from my banks into imports/, a chokidar
  watcher ingests new files using per-bank column maps in mappings.json,
  and rows dedupe on a date+amount+description hash.
- Categorization: ordered regex rules in rules.json run first; unmatched
  transactions land in a review page where one click assigns a category and
  offers to save the pattern as a new rule. Optional LLM fallback, key in
  .env.
- Dashboard: current month spend by category against per-category budgets,
  a 12-month trend line, and top merchants.
- Recurring detection: the same merchant at roughly monthly intervals gets
  flagged as a subscription and listed with its annual cost. This list
  alone tends to pay for the build.
- Accounts and net worth: monthly balance snapshots per account, plotted
  over time.
- Everything local in one SQLite file, localhost only, no telemetry; note
  in the README that the optional LLM call sends transaction text out, skip
  it if that bothers me.
- Out of scope: automatic bank sync (Plaid needs approval and per-connection
  fees) and investment tracking; CSV import is the honest personal version.
- README: how to add a new bank's CSV mapping.
